what: `cairn help` — and the bare `cairn` usage moment — route the asker to the COMPILED help surface (cairnmap), so the system has exactly one help surface and it is derived, never authored. Today bare `cairn` prints an authored name list with no charter text behind it: a second, thinner help surface, which is the exact shape cairnmap exists to collapse.
how_first_cut: A new executable `bin/cmd/help` that execs cairnmap ('a new verb is a new executable in bin/cmd/ — no edit to the dispatcher', the dispatcher's own charter). cairnmap's charter invoke gains `cairn help` so the derivation gate owns the name. The dispatcher's _usage lister stays as the loud-FAILURE surface (its job is the unknown-name moment, not help) but can shrink to the name list plus one pointer line at `cairn help`. /sorted decides the exact cut.
trace: Law 1 + Telos 1 ('what can I do here' with the inference compiled out). Kin, consulted in the lab before this birth: cairn/tools/cairnmap's charter — its `what` IS this answer; no conflict, this is a ROUTE to it. Build-to-the-tool naming: `help` is the one name nobody has to learn.
shape: ASIDE to the cairnmap track (not a new track — it adds a door to a built thing).
falsifier_first_cut: `cairn help` renders the compiled surface; an authored sentence in bin/cairn that duplicates or paraphrases charter content is the defect (falsifier 6 of cairnmap's charter, extended to the dispatcher).
